Industrial Automation

PLC Programming Course for Beginners

Build a strong PLC foundation by understanding the information flow behind automated machines: inputs, program decisions and output commands. The course starts with basic Boolean logic and grows toward practical ladder programming and simulation.

PLC lessons

Lesson 1PLC Basics: Inputs, Outputs & Ladder Logic

Learn Boolean values, scan-cycle concepts, normally open and normally closed instructions, AND logic and OR logic.

Coming nextTags, Addresses & First Practical Program

Build on the first lesson by mapping symbolic tags to real PLC addresses and testing a simple program.

What this course will cover

  1. PLC inputs, outputs and Boolean conditions
  2. Ladder logic contacts, coils and networks
  3. Tags, addresses and I/O mapping
  4. Timers, counters, latches and interlocks
  5. Simulation and troubleshooting
  6. Siemens S7-1200 concepts and practical examples

Electrical wiring, voltage levels and safety requirements depend on the exact hardware. Course examples separate software logic from physical wiring so each can be understood correctly.

PLC programming starts with understanding the machine state

A programmable logic controller reads inputs, evaluates logic and controls outputs in a repeated scan. Learning ladder logic becomes much easier when each contact and coil is connected to a real machine condition instead of memorized as a symbol.

This PLC section is built around practical industrial automation: inputs and outputs, Boolean logic, timers, counters, interlocks, HMI interaction and communication with other devices. Examples are educational and should always be adapted to the actual electrical design and safety requirements of a machine.
